clusters.state_of_play: Andy Burnham, now Prime Minister, faces scrutiny over an undeclared £6,600 Japan party from his time as Manchester Mayor. On his first foreign trip as PM, he traveled to Kyiv for Ukraine's 35th independence day, co-chairing a coalition-of-the-willing meeting, meeting Zelenskyy, playing guitar with Ukrainian soldiers, and announcing UK sharing of classified Storm Shadow missile-component technology and long-range missile blueprints, including support for France in setting up missile assembly lines, to boost Ukraine's missile production. Ukraine has reciprocated with a trove of secret intelligence data to help the UK train troops using AI as part of a landmark military agreement. Burnham has directly challenged Putin over the war's origins, asking 'Who started the fire?', amid Kremlin warnings that the UK is now 'participating in this war,' with a senior Putin adviser threatening a 'semi-military' response and possible attacks on UK drone factories, calling Britain 'evil number one' and declaring that 'Pandora's box has been opened.' Backbenchers have warned Burnham against calling a snap general election. Burnham says he is likely to travel to New York next month for the UN General Assembly, where he plans to meet Donald Trump and lobby, alongside other European leaders, for the US to supply Ukraine with Patriot missiles, calling the current supply problem 'fixable.' He has also said Prince Harry and Meghan's security arrangements are a private matter. Meanwhile, Zelenskyy says Russia plans to draft 300,000 more troops amid reports of increasingly aggressive and intimidating recruitment tactics as Russia prepares for a winter offensive, has warned on the prospect of wartime elections, and declared in a defiant independence day speech that Ukraine wants peace but will not give in to Russia at any price, as Ukrainian drones struck three major Russian retail hubs near Moscow, with Ozon identified as the next targeted economic pressure point, and attempted to strike a military cosmodrome; Ukraine marked the day with a parade featuring robots replacing soldiers. Moscow has since struck a cargo ship in the Black Sea after Zelenskyy called for talks to halt attacks, with Kyiv vowing to bolster regional air defences amid a renewed Black Sea blockade squeezing Ukraine's grain exports and farmers. Separately, the first British national is reported to have been killed fighting for Russia in a drone attack, and Burnham has signalled openness to cut-price tuition fees for EU students as part of a planned EU 'reset' summit. A key Ukraine ally was notably absent from the Kyiv gathering. Trump has dispatched envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv this weekend bearing a fresh US peace plan to end the war, their first visit to Kyiv since Trump's return to office; Moscow is reported to have violated a Zelenskyy-proposed air truce, a drone struck a Ukrainian intelligence (SBU) facility in Kyiv, and Trump said he does not believe Russia intends to attack NATO. The envoys' planned Kremlin meeting with Putin has now taken place, with Putin telling them the situation in Ukraine remains 'difficult,' and both Russia and Ukraine have vowed not to strike each other's capitals for three days during the talks. Russia insisted the US must 'consider realities on the ground,' and Trump said there may be a good chance for a deal. Separately, former MI6 chief John Sawers said enduring peace is unlikely while Putin remains in office and that talks could begin next year.
